speaker: Doctor
text: I am Dr. Agent. I see you have a history of gait and limb ataxia; to begin our evaluation, how long have you been experiencing these balance and coordination issues?

speaker: Patient
text: I started having trouble walking recently, and people say I look drunk when I walk. I also feel clumsy in my arms and legs, especially on the right side.

speaker: Doctor
text: The symptoms of looking "drunk" and feeling clumsy, especially on the right side, suggest a cerebellar issue. Has your condition been getting worse over time, or did it start suddenly? Also, have you noticed any trouble with your speech or swallowing?

speaker: Patient
text: I have Crohn disease and it has been difficult to control. I have been taking natalizumab for about a year.

speaker: Doctor
text: The combination of progressive right-sided ataxia and your history of Crohn's disease treated with natalizumab is highly concerning for Progressive Multifocal Leukoencephalopathy (PML). When did these neurological symptoms first begin relative to starting natalizumab, and have you noticed any visual changes or weakness in your limbs? REQUEST TEST: MRI Brain with contrast.

speaker: Measurement
text: RESULTS: MRI Brain - T1/T2 images showing multifocal demyelinating lesions without gadolinium enhancement, indicative of Progressive Multifocal Leukoencephalopathy (PML).

speaker: Doctor
text: DIAGNOSIS READY: Progressive Multifocal Leukoencephalopathy (PML) secondary to natalizumab therapy. The MRI confirms multifocal demyelinating lesions without enhancement, consistent with JC virus reactivation in an immunocompromised patient.
